title: Identify hot spots for peak-hour crashes (Brevard County, FL, 2010-2015)
output_type: vector (road segments with Gi* z / bins) + map
required_outputs: selected_crash_hotspots.shp (optional file; per-segment results are checked from captured data)
method: Weekday crashes with CRASH_HOD 15-17 (24 746); nearest-edge snap within 1 320 ft (0.25 mi, data in US feet); crash count per road segment (all 69 531 kept); CrashRate = count / (6 * length_ft); Getis-Ord Gi* on CrashRate with the supplied network SWM (inverse network distance, keyed by UniqID), self weight = nearest-neighbour weight, no standardisation, analytical z, FDR-corrected bins.

key_parameters.self_weight: row max (esda star=True default); self weight 1 with inverse weights is degenerate and not accepted

benchmark_defects: '3 pm to 5 pm' is ambiguous (original SQL keeps hours 15, 16 and 17); both readings accepted.

With the SWM's inverse-distance weights (~0.003) the ArcGIS/esda default self weight of 1 makes Gi* equal to the standardised rate (r = 0.9999) - a non-spatial ranking. It is not accepted (UNVERIFIABLE when Gi* + SWM were used): it carries no spatial information.
Workflow text contains a mojibake character (in 'Select Layer By Attribute'); original code refers to 'NwSWM360ft.swm' while the file is 'nwswm360ft.swm' (case).
The benchmark publishes only an ArcPy reference script for this task; no open-source reference script is available.
checks: required: captured peak crash table (24 746 or 16 515 rows, only weekday 15-17 h) or per-segment counts summing to it
required: per-segment count/rate column (69 531 rows) with Pearson >= 0.9 to gold count/rate
required: per-segment z-like column with Pearson >= 0.9 to a Gi(*) variant computed on the supplied network SWM
self-weight-dominated Gi* variants excluded; candidates with r >= 0.95 to the plain count/rate rejected (UNVERIFIABLE if Gi*+SWM used in that convention)
optional: map colours drawn from the Gi column
